claims.claim_text: Fetches and parses the HTML content of a website
claims.reason: Whether the agent correctly fetches and parses HTML is a behavioral claim about its internal processing, not directly verifiable by an oracle measuring the output fact.

claims.claim_text: Reports the page title
claims.reason: The oracle can retrieve the page title and compare it to what the agent reports.

claims.claim_text: Reports the meta description tag
claims.reason: The oracle can retrieve the meta description and compare it to what the agent reports.

claims.claim_text: Reports the meta keywords tag
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures the meta keywords tag content.

claims.claim_text: Reports a list of headings (h1-h6)
claims.reason: The oracle can check h1 presence/count; h2-h6 are not covered but h1 is partially verifiable.

claims.claim_text: Reports a list of internal and external links
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures link lists from a page.

claims.claim_text: Reports a list of images with alt text
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures image alt text.

claims.claim_text: Reports the main text content (first 5000 characters)
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures extracted text content from a page.

claims.claim_text: Reports the HTTP status code
claims.reason: The oracle can retrieve the HTTP status code and compare it to what the agent reports.

claims.claim_text: Reports the content length (size of the page)
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures page content length/size.

claims.claim_text: Reports whether schema markup is present
claims.reason: The oracle checks for JSON-LD structured data presence, which covers schema markup detection.

claims.claim_text: Reports the HTML lang attribute
claims.reason: The oracle retrieves the HTML lang attribute and can be compared to what the agent reports.

claims.claim_text: Analyzes page speed and performance metrics for a website
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures page speed or performance metrics.

claims.claim_text: Checks if a website is mobile-friendly
claims.reason: The oracle checks for the viewport meta tag, a key mobile-friendliness signal.

claims.claim_text: Extracts all meta tags from a website
claims.reason: No oracle covers all meta tags; only meta description is in the catalog, so full extraction cannot be verified.

claims.claim_text: Analyzes site structure, navigation, and internal linking
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog measures site structure, navigation, or internal linking analysis.

claims.claim_text: Checks robots.txt permissions for AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, etc.)
claims.reason: The oracle only checks robots.txt existence and blanket disallow; per-bot permission checking is not covered by any catalog oracle.

claims.claim_text: Checks for the presence of /llms.txt
claims.reason: The oracle directly checks for the presence of /llms.txt at the origin.

claims.claim_text: Performs deep analysis of Schema.org JSON-LD structured data
claims.reason: The oracle only checks presence of JSON-LD; deep analysis of its content is not verifiable by any catalog oracle.

claims.claim_text: Identifies which Schema.org types are present on a page
claims.reason: The oracle only checks JSON-LD presence, not which Schema.org types are used; type identification cannot be verified.

claims.claim_text: Counts FAQ questions and HowTo steps in schema markup
claims.reason: No oracle in the catalog counts FAQ questions or HowTo steps in schema markup.

claims.claim_text: Scores AEO (Agent Engine Optimization) value of schema markup
claims.reason: AEO scoring is a subjective/invented score with no independent oracle to verify it.

claims.claim_text: Identifies missing high-value Schema.org types
claims.reason: Identifying missing schema types is a subjective recommendation not verifiable by any catalog oracle.

claims.claim_text: Analyzes content structure for AI readability and LLM retrieval quality
claims.reason: AI readability and LLM retrieval quality are subjective assessments with no catalog oracle to verify them.

claims.claim_text: Exposes an A2A endpoint at https://searchopti.cloud/a2a/jsonrpc
claims.reason: The oracle checks whether something is serving at this URL, verifying the A2A endpoint claim.

claims.claim_text: Exposes an MCP tool endpoint at https://searchopti.cloud/mcp
claims.reason: The oracle checks whether something is serving at this URL, verifying the MCP endpoint claim.

claims.claim_text: Supports streaming responses
claims.reason: Streaming support is a protocol/transport capability checkable by contract (e.g., chunked transfer encoding or SSE), not by a content oracle.
